verbalization: Phytolaccoside B appears to exert its biological effects through a multi-step mechanism involving the glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) enzyme. The evidence suggests that Phytolaccoside B targets the mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase 13 (MAP3K13) protein, which in turn is a target of Isoswinholide B. This chain of interactions ultimately leads to the inhibition of GAPDH. The integration of these pathways implies that Phytolaccoside B may act as a modulator of the MAP3K13 signaling cascade, which is involved in cellular stress responses and metabolic regulation. The observed scores suggest a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, but further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the direct interaction between Phytolaccoside B and GAPDH. The mechanism highlights the potential for Phytolaccoside B to influence metabolic pathways through its interaction with MAP3K13, underscoring its role in cellular processes that are regulated by this enzyme.
